title: Nager.Date public holidays API (Italy, national holidays)
summary: REST API returning public-holiday dates per year and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. For IT it returns national holidays only (13 entries per year in the probes for 2024 and 2025), one record per date with English and local names and a global flag. Grain is one record per holiday per day, not a time series of counts; it can serve only as a calendar covariate for the daily clinic-count need (N4) in the production window, and it does not supply any clinic counts, air quality, traffic or weather.

spatial.notes: National holidays only in the IT probes (global=true for all sampled entries, counties null). Regional patron-saint days and local closures are not visible in the probes.

access.request_process: GET https://date.nager.at/api/v3/PublicHolidays/{year}/{country}; no key observed in probes

documentation_excerpts: Register param_notes: 'country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (PT, GB, FR, ...).'
README (GitHub): 'Easily access public holidays for 200+ countries via .NET, REST API, Docker, or NuGet'; 'MIT license'.
README: hosted REST API at nagerholidays.com; self-hosted Docker variant uses /api/v4/Holidays/{country}/{year} (v4 path differs from the v3 path in the register).
quality_notes: Probe for IT 2025 returned 13 holidays, dates 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-26 (probe shape only shows 3 items plus '10 more'); probe for IT 2024 returned 13 holidays, dates 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-26. Both probes returned byte-identical sized responses (2307 bytes) and were served from cache.
Covers national holidays only; regional or local closures (e.g. patron-saint days, municipal closures of Valdena) are not covered, so the calendar is incomplete for a city-level covariate.
Register path template (/api/v3/PublicHolidays/{year}/{country}) differs from the self-hosted README example (/api/v4/Holidays/...). The probed v3 path works; API version stability not confirmed.
Register terms_url points to the GitHub repository (software MIT licence), not to a data-licence statement; the API's own terms were not read.
Calendar is a covariate only: it does not satisfy N4 (daily respiratory clinic counts by district); those must come from the city clinic data.

Self-hosted README documents a v4 path, and the register uses v3
